raw_case_text:
A 20 year old Saudi male was diagnosed to have severe acquired AA at King Faisal Specialist Hospital and Research Centre (KFSH&RC) in Riyadh on 9/4/2006. He presented with 2 week history of low grade pyrexia, mucosal bleeding and anemic symptoms and his physical examination revelaed: pallor, few ecchymotic areas over the limbs, no external lymphadenopathy, a clear chest, no palpable abdominal organomegaly, and normal cardiovascular and neurological systems. Complete blood count (CBC) showed: WBC: 1.5 x 109/L with neutrophils of 0.02, Hb: 72 g/L and PLT: 5 x 109/L. Blood film revealed severe neutropenia and thrombocytopenia but no blast cells and bone marrow biopsy showed a hypocellular marrow with no blasts and a normal cytogenetic analysis. Renal, hepatic and coagulation profiles were normal. Screens for fanconi anemia, paroxysmal nocturnal hemoglobinuria, hepatitis, brucellosis, syphilis, viruses and autoimmune disorders were all negative. The patient was given supportive measures and after identifying an HLA identical and a healthy sibling donor, prepartions for allogeneic HSCT were made. The transplant conditioning was composed of fludarabine and cyclophophamide. The patient received acyclovir, fluconazole and trimethoprim-sulphamethoxazole (TMP/SMZ) as infection prophylaxis and cyclosporine-A and methotrexate as graft versus host disease (GVHD) prophylaxis. On 15/5/2006, the patient was given his allograft without any complication. The patient developed: grade I mucositis treated with IV morphine infusion and few febrile neutropenic episodes treated empirically with vancomycin, cefepime, amphotericin-B and metronidazole. However, no acute GVHD, cytomegalovirus infection, venoocclusive disease of the liver or hemorrhagic cystitis were encountered. The patient engrafted his leucocytes on day +24 and his platelets on day +16 HSCT. After the recovery of his blood counts, the patient was discharged on zantac, cyclosporine-A and prophylactic antimicrobials.
On 4/9/2006, he presented with 2 week history of high grade pyrexia, rigors and sweating. He denied intake of raw milk. Physical examination did not reveal any abnormality. CBC showed: WBC: 2.37 x 109/L with neutrophils of 1.59, Hb: 152 g/L and PLT: 97 x 109/L. Serum creatinine was 130 mumol/l [normal range: 0-122 mumole/L], bilirubin 30 mumol/L [normal range: 0-22 mumole/L], ALT: 194 U/L [normal range: 0-50 U/L], AST: 176 U/L [normal range: 0-40 U/L]. Blood cultures grew Brucella melitensis sensitive to: TMP/SMZ, streptomycin, tetracyclin, ciprofloxacin and imipenem. Brucella serology was strongly positive with 2-mercaptoethanol titer of 1:1280 and agglutination antibody titer of 1:20480. Initially, the patient was given streptomycin 1 gram intramuscularly twice daily and ciprofloxacin 400 mg orally twice daily for two weeks. Few days later, the clinical manifestation of brucellosis disappeared then the blood counts started to recover so streptomycin was replaced by doxycyline 100 mg orally twice daily and the patient was continued on ciprofloxacin for 4 more weeks. Subsequently, the blood cultures for Brucella became negative, the Brucella titers decreased significantly, the blood indices as well as the renal and the hepatic profiles normalized. When the patient was last seen on 29/4/2008, he was asymptomatic and his physical examination did not reveal any abnormality. CBC showed: WBC: 6.13 x 109/L with neutrophilis of 2.82, Hb: 142 g/L and PLT: 186 x 109/L. The renal and the hepatic profiles were normal. No new medication was prescribed and the patient was given a new follow up appointment.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 20-year-old male post-allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplant presented with a 2-week history of high-grade pyrexia, rigors, and sweating.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: The patient had severe acquired aplastic anemia diagnosed in April 2006 and underwent successful HLA-identical sibling allogeneic HSCT on 15/5/2006 following fludarabine and cyclophosphamide conditioning, with leukocyte engraftment on day +24 and platelet engraftment on day +16. On 4/9/2006, he presented with a 2-week history of high-grade pyrexia, rigors, and profuse sweating. He denied consuming raw milk.
subjective.past_medical_history: Severe acquired aplastic anemia diagnosed on 9/4/2006 (bone marrow biopsy showed hypocellular marrow without blasts and normal cytogenetics; baseline screens for Fanconi anemia, PNH, hepatitis, syphilis, brucellosis, and autoantibodies negative). Underwent allogeneic HSCT on 15/5/2006. Conditioning: fludarabine and cyclophosphamide. Prophylaxis: acyclovir, fluconazole, trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole (TMP/SMZ), cyclosporine-A, and methotrexate. Post-transplant course complicated by grade I mucositis (treated with IV morphine) and febrile neutropenia (treated empirically with vancomycin, cefepime, amphotericin B, and metronidazole). Discharged on ranitidine (Zantac), cyclosporine-A, and prophylactic antimicrobials. Epidemiological exposure: denied ingestion of raw milk.
subjective.review_of_systems: Reports high-grade pyrexia, rigors, and sweating. Denies consumption of raw milk. Current medications: ranitidine, cyclosporine-A, and prophylactic antimicrobials.

objective.physical_examination: Physical examination on 4/9/2006 was completely unremarkable (clear chest, no organomegaly, no lymphadenopathy, normal cardiovascular and neurological systems). Baseline examination on 9/4/2006 showed pallor and few limb ecchymoses.
objective.routine_investigations: At presentation on 4/9/2006: WBC 2.37 x 10^9/L (neutrophils 1.59 x 10^9/L), hemoglobin: 152 g/L, platelet count: 97 x 10^9/L. Serum creatinine: 130 mumol/L (normal range 0-122 mumol/L), total bilirubin: 30 mumol/L (normal range 0-22 mumol/L), ALT: 194 U/L (normal range 0-50 U/L), AST: 176 U/L (normal range 0-40 U/L). Initial pre-transplant CBC (9/4/2006): WBC 1.5 x 10^9/L (neutrophils 0.02), Hb 72 g/L, platelets 5 x 10^9/L; blood film showed severe neutropenia and thrombocytopenia without blast cells. Follow-up CBC on 29/4/2008: WBC 6.13 x 10^9/L (neutrophils 2.82), Hb 142 g/L, platelets 186 x 10^9/L; renal and hepatic profiles normalized.
objective.advanced_workup: Pre-transplant bone marrow biopsy demonstrated a hypocellular marrow without blasts and normal cytogenetic analysis. Susceptibility testing of the isolated pathogen showed susceptibility to TMP/SMZ, streptomycin, tetracycline, ciprofloxacin, and imipenem.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: Confirmation: Blood cultures grew Brucella melitensis sensitive to TMP/SMZ, streptomycin, tetracycline, ciprofloxacin, and imipenem. Brucella serology was strongly positive with a 2-mercaptoethanol titer of 1:1,280 and an agglutination antibody titer of 1:20,480. Differential diagnosis: Viral infections (hepatitis viruses, CMV), syphilis, Fanconi anemia, PNH, and autoimmune disorders ruled out by pre-transplant workup; acute GVHD and veno-occlusive disease excluded. Management and Outcome: Initially treated with intramuscular streptomycin 1 g twice daily and oral ciprofloxacin 400 mg twice daily for 2 weeks. Following clinical resolution and hematological recovery, streptomycin was discontinued and oral doxycycline 100 mg twice daily was started, with oral ciprofloxacin continued for an additional 4 weeks (total 6 weeks). Blood cultures became negative, Brucella antibody titers dropped significantly, and blood counts, renal function, and liver enzymes normalized. At follow-up on 29/4/2008, the patient remained fully asymptomatic with normal examination, normal blood counts, and normal hepatic and renal function.
